text: The Bear is an American comedy-drama series created by Christopher Storer for FX on Hulu. Jeremy Allen White stars as Carmy Berzatto, a talented chef who returns to his hometown of Chicago to manage the chaotic kitchen at his deceased brother's Italian beef sandwich shop, leaving behind his career in Michelin-starred restaurants. The regular cast includes Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Ayo Edebiri, Lionel Boyce, Liza Colón-Zayas, Abby Elliott, Matty Matheson, and Edwin Lee Gibson. The series premiered on FX on Hulu on June 23, 2022, with all episodes of the first season released on that date; the second season followed on June 22, 2023. In November 2023, the series was renewed for a third season, released on June 26, 2024, and in March 2024, it was renewed for a fourth season, which premiered on June 25, 2025. In July 2025, the series was renewed for a fifth season. The show's storyline is divided into parts marked by onscreen title cards, with Part II appearing in the first episode of season 2 and Part III in the first episode of season 3, which concluded with a "to be continued" card. Most episodes are about 30 minutes long, ranging from 20 minutes to 70 minutes. FX ordered a pilot in March 2021, written and directed by Christopher Storer, and then ordered the series in October 2021 for a 2022 premiere. The sandwich shop interior is modeled after Mr. Beef on Orleans Street in River North, a shop frequently visited by Storer, who is a friend of Christopher Zucchero, the current owner. The show's culinary production is overseen by co-executive producer Courtney Storer (sister of Christopher Storer) and culinary co-producer C. J. Capace, with additional team members including chefs Justin Selk, Nicole Biyani, Danielle Stefanick, Gabriel Wallace, Jeffrey Thomas, and Brian Lockwood. The lead costume designer is Courtney Wheeler, with Lariana Santiago as assistant; Ally Vickers leads the hair department; Laura Roeper (sister of Chicago Sun-Times critic Richard Roeper) is the Chicago-based prop master; Merje Veski is the production designer; Lisa Korpan is the art director; and Eric Frankel heads the set decoration department. The primary cinematographer is Andrew Wehde, with A-camera operator Gary Malouf and B-camera operator Chris Dame having worked with Storer and Wehde previously; Scott D. Smith has led the sound mixing team since the pilot, Steve "Major" Giammaria is the supervising sound editor, and Evan Benjamin is the dialogue sound editor; the episode cuts are handled by Joanna Naugle, Adam Epstein, and Megan Mancini. The show's soundtrack features 1980s to 2000s alternative and mainstream rock songs, including tracks by Wilco, Radiohead, Van Morrison, Pearl Jam, Sufjan Stevens, John Mayer, Refused, The Breeders, Erasure, The Replacements, Counting Crows, Genesis, Nine Inch Nails, John Mellencamp, R.E.M., Weezer, The Smashing Pumpkins, Led Zeppelin, Oasis, and Taylor Swift (with "Love Story (Taylor's Version)", "Long Live (Taylor's Version)", and "Style (Taylor's Version)"), selected by Storer and executive producer Josh Senior. The primary composers are Chicago-based Jeffrey "JQ" Qaiyum and Johnny Iguana, whose instrumentals are used primarily in back-of-house scenes; Iguana described JQ as a "wizard producer" who creates the beats and handles the chords and notes. The Bear premiered in the U.S. on June 23, 2022, and became available internationally on Disney+'s Star hub; it was also accessible on Hulu via Disney+ in the U.S. starting December 6, 2023. The series has received critical acclaim, with a 93% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and an 83 out of 100 score on Metacritic. The first season earned a 100% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes with a Metacritic score of 88; the second season received 99% positive reviews and a Metacritic score of 92; the third season had an 89% approval rating and a Metacritic score of 80; the fourth season received an 84% approval rating and a Metacritic score of 72. The American Film Institute named it one of the ten best television programs of the year in both 2022 and 2023, and The Guardian ranked it number one of the best 100 TV shows of 2022, calling it "the best workplace drama since Mad Men." It appeared on numerous "Best of 2022" and "Best of 2023" lists. The show was the most-nominated series in comedy categories at the 2024 Emmys with 23 nominations, surpassing 30 Rock's 22 from 2009, but lost the Outstanding Comedy Series award to Hacks, with industry observers suggesting voter resentment over its lack of comedic content. Reelgood and JustWatch reported that The Bear was among the most-streamed programs in the U.S., with peak viewership during July 2024 and 2025, and it was the most-watched comedy series in FX history for its first season and the most-watched season premiere in the network's history for its second season. The season 3 premiere garnered 5.4 million views in its first four days, making it the most-watched season premiere for any scripted series on Hulu and the best FX premiere on Hulu, with 1,233 million minutes of viewing recorded from June 24–30, surpassing the previous peak of 1.01 billion minutes. The Bear was the third most-streamed show in the U.S. in 2024 and the second most-streamed in Canada that year.
